TestAuth::test_transitional_auth_from_de.description: 3-node cluster starts with AllowAll auth, then full rolling restart to TransitionalAuthenticator/TransitionalAuthorizer, then to strict PasswordAuthenticator/CassandraAuthorizer. In transitional mode: wrong credentials log in as anonymous, anonymous may CREATE KEYSPACE/TABLE/SELECT but is refused LIST USERS/GRANT/REVOKE, while connecting without any credentials fails with AuthenticationFailed. After switching to strict auth: no-creds and wrong-pwd logins fail, the user created during transition logs in and has no SELECT/AUTHORIZE perms. Guards the documented zero-downtime 'enable auth' migration path via com.scylladb.auth.Transitional*.

TestAuth::test_transitional_auth_from_pw.description: 3-node cluster starts with PasswordAuthenticator/CassandraAuthorizer, creates user 'normal' (LIST USERS shows only itself), checks wrong-pwd is rejected; then rolling restart to Transitional auth: authenticated normal can LIST USERS, CREATE KEYSPACE/TABLE but is refused GRANT/REVOKE (no AUTHORIZE), wrong-pwd logs in as anonymous, no-credentials is rejected. Finally switches to AllowAll and verifies all logins become anonymous. Covers the 'reverse' (disable auth) transition order.

TestAuth::test_auth_username_password_pa.description: Starts 3-node cluster with PasswordAuthenticator/CassandraAuthorizer and auth_superuser_name='gris' + auth_superuser_salted_password (sha512 of 'gris'). Asserts no-creds, unknown user, and right-user/wrong-password logins fail with AuthenticationFailed, that 'gris'/'gris' logs in as superuser and can CREATE USER/KEYSPACE/TABLE, and that the new user has no SELECT/AUTHORIZE. Guards the config-driven default superuser feature from scylladb PR #12214.

TestAuth::test_certificate_auth.description: Single node with CQL TLS (require_client_auth=True), com.scylladb.auth.CertificateAuthenticator + CassandraAuthorizer, auth_superuser_name='admin' and auth_certificate_role_queries [ALTNAME EMAIL=(\w+)@scylladb.com, SUBJECT CN=([^,]+)]. Asserts: no client cert and certs for non-existent roles (client1/2/3) are refused; admin cert logs in as superuser; after CREATE USER client2 its CN-cert logs in, has no SELECT/AUTHORIZE, others still refused; after CREATE USER client3 the email-SAN cert (ALTNAME query) logs in. Guards the CertificateAuthenticator feature from scylladb PR #12214.
